issues.legal_issue: A later regime establishing an exclusive state monopoly over trade in minor forest produce makes inconsistent declarations and injunctions inoperative.
material_facts: A court had declared that certain residents could sell minor forest produce to buyers of their choice and had granted an injunction preventing interference with that right.
After that judgment, a regulation came into force covering the relevant scheduled areas and minor forest produce, reserving the specified trade exclusively to a designated corporation.
The regulation prohibited other persons from selling, purchasing, collecting, processing, storing, or transporting the covered produce.
issues.conclusion: The declaration and injunction could not stand in view of the regulation and were vacated; the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Andhra Pradesh Regulation 1 of 1979, made under paragraph 5(2) of the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution, created a state monopoly in the trade of specified minor forest produce in scheduled areas. Section 2(d) defined the grower; section 3 permitted appointment of the corporation as the government’s agent; and section 4 reserved the specified activities to the corporation and allowed growers to sell to it in the prescribed manner. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_challenges_prior_relief: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a declaration or injunction granted earlier.
predicates.exclusive_trade_regime_applies: A later operative legal regime applies to the relevant area and produce and reserves the covered trade exclusively to a designated corporation.
predicates.prior_relief_permits_competing_trade: The challenged relief permits private persons to sell the produce to buyers other than the designated corporation and prevents interference with that activity.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges earlier relief that permits competing trade, and an operative exclusive-trade regime applies, the earlier relief is vacated.
